scope: Ubuntu Wayland reference host for host-neutral pointer coalescing/prediction, touch force normalization, bounded built-in-host transport, independent multi-window ownership, hardware GPU presentation/device-loss recovery and the AccessKit AT-SPI adapter

checks.name: pointer_motion_coalescing
checks.replacement: The latest consecutive Move/Hover sample replaces the pending sample for the same pointer identity; lifecycle and non-pointer events flush it first.

checks.name: linux_touch_normalization
checks.replacement: winit Touch maps to Down/Move/Up/Cancel with stable touch identity; calibrated or normalized force is clamped to 0..=1; the first contact remains primary until it ends.

checks.name: host_neutral_motion_prediction
checks.replacement: PointerMotionPredictor uses host timestamps for advisory linear extrapolation and resets velocity on pointer identity changes or lifecycle events.

checks.name: built_in_host_inbox_contract
checks.replacement: HostInbox enforces authenticated session/epoch, exact sequence, bounded backpressure, returned rejection payloads and permanent close. The host_loopback example crosses scene update, CPU frame, backpressure and retirement without winit/wgpu.

checks.name: hardware_gpu_surface_present
checks.note: A real hardware adapter rendered into the compositor-owned Wayland Surface, acknowledged the present, executed the host recovery lifecycle drill, recreated device/Surface/renderer generation 2, and presented again.

checks.name: hardware_gpu_suspend_resume
checks.note: Engine suspend, host window/device/Surface recreation, engine resume and second hardware present all completed.

checks.name: accesskit_winit_atspi_window
checks.cleanup: The temporary toolkit-accessibility enablement was restored to false after verification.

checks.name: cross_target_host_neutral_core_check
checks.note: cargo check --locked succeeded for the host-neutral core on every target and for desktop-accessibility/example-window on Windows x86_64 plus macOS x86_64/AArch64. Android AArch64 and iOS AArch64 core targets also compile. These are compile boundary checks, not runtime acceptance.

checks.name: gpu_device_loss_recovery
checks.hardware_drill: RTX 3060 Vulkan: frame 1 presented, host recovery event handled, device/Surface/renderer generation 2 created, frame 2 presented
checks.callback_test: VM wgpu test destroyed the device and observed DeviceLostReason::Destroyed
checks.note: The hardware drill routes through the same host lifecycle without claiming a driver-induced hardware loss.

cross_platform_boundary.engine_contract: PointerMotionCoalescer, PointerMotionPredictor, HostInbox and the normalized input model contain no window-system types.
cross_platform_boundary.linux_adapter: winit Touch plus the AccessKit winit AT-SPI adapter.
cross_platform_boundary.other_platforms: The same optional accesskit_winit dependency selects UIA, macOS, Android or iOS at compile time. No Windows, macOS or mobile runtime acceptance is claimed from Ubuntu.

test_results.default_cargo_test: passed: 146 library tests plus all default integration tests and doctest
test_results.default_all_targets_check: passed, including host_loopback and multiwindow examples
test_results.host_loopback: 1 passed; example output host_loopback=pass session=41 epoch=3 version=2
test_results.platform_input: 3 passed: pen axes, invalid ranges and pressure fallback

limits: The application requested FIFO/Vsync and the hardware Surface accepted it; compositor-specific vblank deadline latency was not measured.
The hardware run used the host recovery drill rather than a driver-induced loss. A separate VM test destroys the wgpu device and observes the real DeviceLostReason::Destroyed callback.
Only winit force normalization is covered; raw pen tilt, twist, barrel rotation and device-specific pressure curves are not claimed.
The multi-window example preserves engine state while host Window/Surface objects are recreated; a real OS session suspend was not triggered in this run.
AT-SPI was activated temporarily; screen-reader navigation was not exercised.
The jasper-os built-in host is not part of this reference-host report.
